News.title: Mayors to get powers to overrule local councils on planning decisions
News.content:
Mayors across England will be given new powers to overrule local councils on some planning decisions.

The change would apply to proposals with more than 150 homes, more than 15,000 square metres of commercial space or buildings over 30 metres.

Mayors in 13 areas including Manchester, Liverpool, the West of England and the West Midlands will gain similar powers to Sir Sadiq Khan in London, who is already able to "call in" planning decisions.

Housing minister Matthew Pennycook said the powers were an "essential part of the toolkit that mayors need to effectively deliver new homes and regeneration".

The Conservatives questioned whether it was right for councils to lose the "ability to make planning decisions in their own communities".

The powers will also be available to mayors in the Combined Authorities in North East England, South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, York and North Yorkshire, Hull and East Yorkshire, Greater Lincolnshire, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, East Midlands, and Tees Valley.

Paul Bristow, the Conservative mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, told BBC Breakfast that if he had local powers, he would approve "tomorrow" a couple of blocked schemes that he said would "get new homes built that families could move into and charge economic growth".

Bristow said "it's not about overriding what local people want", but about developers and councils finding a compromise on projects instead of just saying no - which he believed the "perceived threat of intervention" would help.

In London, where Khan already has the power to review decisions on certain developments, external, housebuilding has fallen in recent years. But Pennycook insisted the "call in" powers had helped the mayor "unblock strategic growth sites" in the capital.

Bristow said if he had a similar local plan it would be "much more light touch" than London.

In the 2024 general election, the Labour government promised to build 1.5 million homes in England by the end of the decade, but housebuilders have warned the target could be missed.

Pennycook said the government was "absolutely determined to stick with that ambition".

He acknowledged the target was "really stretching" but said nearly 180,000 children were in temporary accommodation and "any smaller target wouldn't be commensurate with the scale of the challenge".

Bristow said the government has "no chance whatsoever" to meet its 1.5 million target.

"We need economic growth in this country, we need to get building and families need places to live, and at the moment, the planning system just isn't working."

In addition to gaining the new "call-in" powers, mayors are set to be able to grant "up-front permission", which the government says will allow building to begin "without a developer having to apply".

A consultation on how the powers will work is due to be published next week.

The government has sought to stress that local councils will continue to decide the majority of applications and that all decisions must still follow planning rules.

It has also said mayors will get a "bigger say" over how housing funding is spent in their area, with the government directing national agency Homes England to focus on local mayors' priorities.

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who served as mayor for Greater Manchester for nearly a decade, has repeatedly expressed his desire to transfer more powers to local mayors.

"Challenge does need to be made to local decision-making and actually it cuts both ways," he told the Sunday Times.

"Sometimes it's the other way round. It's the local authority putting forward something that's unacceptable in terms of the impact on the community. It's a two-way street."

Last month, Burnham promised to give all mayors a share of income tax revenue, saying he wanted to "bring power home" to "every postcode".

Earlier this week, he announced a secondment programme to send high-performing civil servants to work in mayoral offices.

The approach has faced criticism from some in his own party and the Liberal Democrats, who fear it could create a "two-tier system" that discriminates against those areas that do not have an elected mayor.

News.title: CrossCountry cancels 'almost all' UK services after power cut
News.content:
Trains across the UK have been cancelled by rail operator CrossCountry after a power cut at its control centre.

The power outage started in Birmingham on Saturday and as a result, many of the systems used to manage the railway are unavailable, the operator said.

Cancellations are affecting most routes, from Glasgow to Penzance and Leeds to Manchester, until further notice because of "significant and unforeseen disruption", said CrossCountry, ranked Britain's worst rail operator, in June.

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said she was "concerned to hear about a power outage" and had asked publicly owned operators to provide "extra services where possible".

"We've also sent Network Rail power teams who are onsite and working to restore power and systems as soon as possible," she added.

Passengers are venting their anger on social media, saying the situation is the "worst case scenario" at the weekend, with some taking coaches before continuing their train journey with another operator.

Major routes between Manchester and Birmingham, which passes through Stoke-on-Trent, Coventry and Wolverhampton, along with routes from Leeds to York, Cheltenham to Cardiff and Glasgow to Edinburgh, are all affected.

CrossCountry confirmed tickets for Sunday would remain valid until Wednesday.

One user on X asked the operator if the situation would be resolved on Monday.

It responded: "We would hope so, but at the moment we have no further updates."

News.title: How a new era of heatwaves could shake up the school calendar
News.content:
Over the past two weeks, the sound of children has returned to Scotland's school playgrounds. Their summer breaks began in late June or early July and ended in mid-August.

It's an academic year replicated in other European countries too.

In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, however, children will not return until early September. Their holidays are a similar length to Scotland's but England and Wales schools did not break up until late July, something that meant pupils were in school during the peak of the early summer heat.

Or at least they were meant to be in school. While it was 30C or more outside, inside many classrooms it felt far hotter. With no air conditioning and limited ventilation, the heat became stifling and more than 1,000 schools across the UK either closed or sent pupils home early before the hottest part of the afternoon. Conditions were particularly challenging for GCSE and Aâlevel students sitting exams during extreme heat.

Baroness Brown, chair of the UK's Climate Change Adaptation committee, has warned that "we know high temperatures can significantly impair concentration and performance" of children in schools.

Back in February 2026, Ofsted's chief inspector Sir Martyn Oliver said the timing of the school holidays should be reconsidered: "It's pretty hot usually in May, June and July, just at the point you're asking children to sit down and take an examâ¦ so I think there is a need to have a good old look at it [the school year]."

The recent hot weather has seen some parents join his call. Andrea Bigger, a parent in London, is "absolutely aware of the dangers" of extreme heat in classrooms. She says her daughter has previously suffered from heat exhaustion and was hospitalised after overheating at her primary school. She is "really concerned that the UK is not ready or prepared for this".

And this summer was not a one off. BBC analysis of temperature data shows a clear shift. In the 1960s, the first 30C day was occurring on average on 13 July. In the 2020s that figure has been 19 June.

News.title: Why we can't look away from hoarder home clean-ups
News.content:
Gordon says the main reason she posts online is to raise awareness, particularly about hoarding disorder and mental health.

According to the NHS, hoarding disorder is a mental health condition, external in which someone collects a lot of things and finds it difficult to get rid of them, even when they negatively affect their daily life.

"I think it's really easy to be quite judgmental," she says.

"People see footage of these homes online and in documentaries, and it's really easy to judge and think the person's lazy.

"There's a lot of stigma behind it and a lot of misunderstanding."

She says the stigma of being a hoarder can stop people from seeking help.

"This is real life. It's mental health. It's people who are finding themselves living in really unsafe, unsanitary conditions through no fault of their own.

"The more we can talk about it, the better. The less we judge, the more we can understand, [and that] is only going to be a good thing."

Gordon says many of her followers are hoarders themselves.

"I get a lot of messages in my inbox saying, 'Thank you so much for your content. That house that you did last week, mine's not dissimilar to that and you're making me feel like I'm not the only one that lives like this'.

"A lot of people have messaged me and said that, because they've seen my videos, they found the courage to ask for help or maybe hire a cleaner.

"So it is having a really positive effect."

Listen to highlights from Lincolnshire on BBC Sounds and Hull and East Yorkshire on BBC Sounds, and watch the latest episode of Look North.

News.title: Trump Mobile promoted a 'Made in the USA' phone - but the details kept changing
News.content:
When Trump Mobile was launched by US President Donald Trump's eldest sons in the summer of 2025, the company advertised that a "T1" smartphone would be built in the US and shipped to customers within months.

Over the last year, key details about the phone's manufacture, design and delivery date have changed, and some customers are still waiting for their phones - as Thomas Copeland explains.

News.title: Did a goat herder's lucky $200 nugget spark a gold rush in western Kenya?
News.content:
A goat herder from a remote area of western Kenya has told the BBC his discovery of a golden nugget has sparked a gold rush, overwhelming his small village over the last few weeks.

When people found out that 33-year-old Manasse Lomachar had sold his three grams of gold for 36,000 Kenyan shillings ($280; Â£205) several weeks ago, he believes this led to the arrival of thousands of prospectors in Cheporor.

And it is true that what last month was just bushland and rough grazing ground near the village is now scarred by pits, mounds of earth and makeshift mining camps.

It is not clear if was Lomachar's lucky find or other recent discoveries that sparked the excitement. But local authorities estimate that about 10,000 people arrived at the height of the rush.

Even a small amount of the precious metal can transform the futures of these men and women - from Kenya and neighbouring Uganda - many of whose precarious lives rest on an unreliable farming income.

News.title: Robot boxing, football and sprinting at World Humanoid Games
News.content:
The second-edition of the World Humanoid Games is under way in China.

The competition, which kicked off on Saturday, will run for five days and has already included a robot running faster than Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record.

Elsewhere at the event in Beijing, a robot performed Cristiano Ronaldo's iconic 'Siuuu' celebration on the football pitch and droids took part in synchronised marching at its opening ceremony.

Robots have also been competing in events including boxing, high jump, Tai Chi and table tennis.

The BBC's China correspondent Stephen McDonell reports from the country's capital.

News.title: Plan to restrict serious offenders to certain areas to start in October
News.content:
A scheme that could see serious sexual and violent offenders confined to areas just a few miles wide after leaving prison will be launched in October, Justice Secretary Alex Norris has announced.

Government ministers say this is designed to give victims greater freedom and further reduce the possibility of unwanted contact

The intention to introduce "restriction zones" for violent offenders who leave prison and who are on probation was first announced by the government last year.

Probation officers will be able to limit where serious offenders can go for as long as it is deemed necessary. Those who breach their new boundaries could be recalled to prison.

This would go beyond the current practice of imposing "exclusion zones" which ban offenders from specific locations such as a victim's home or place of work.

Norris is expected to come up with proposals to further restrict the early release of some prisoners when Parliament resumes next month.

But the Conservatives say that the best thing Labour could do to protect victims is to bring forward emergency legislation which would stop the early release of thousands of criminals.

There is a risk that serious sexual and violent offenders and victims could encounter one another outside exclusion zones.

The new scheme will specify confined areas for offenders in plans tailored to them and developed in consultation with victims.

Norris said the scheme would use GPS technology monitored by probation officers so that "those who step outside the boundaries can be quickly identified and face being sent back to prison".

"Offenders should carry the consequences of their crimes, not their victims," he added.

Amy Glover, director of domestic abuse services at Advance, a charity supporting women and girls who have experienced domestic abuse, praised the "change in focus".

However, she also called for reform to the criminal justice system saying many survivors of abuse chose "not to pursue a criminal conviction, and for those that do only 5% reach conviction."

A domestic abuse survivor named only as Kristina called the restriction zones a "fantastic concept" but noted that a perpetrator had continuously breached her indefinite restraining order "without consequence".

"The biggest challenge would be to gain victims' confidence in authorities to follow through their promises of protection," she added.

The announcement of the restriction zone scheme's start date comes after a change to the government's early release scheme following a backlash.

Introduced to ease prison overcrowding, on 4 August the policy was updated so people sentenced for rape, serious child sex offences and grooming would not be eligible for early release.

The Prison Governors' association warned this change to plans at a "very late stage" put further pressure on prison staff.

The restriction zone scheme was criticised when it was announced last year for potentially putting pressure on probation staff, something the government says it hopes to alleviate with more staff and a greater use of technology.

If you are suffering from domestic abuse, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line

News.title: Struggling households need more help with bills, energy industry says
News.content:
Higher energy bills this winter mean the government should step in to provide more help for households most in need, the body representing energy firms in the UK has said.

Stubbornly high prices over the last few years have left some people needing "emergency support" over and above the existing Â£150 Warm Home Discount, Energy UK said.

A "better targeted" support scheme that takes into account someone's income, health and energy consumption was needed, it added.

On Wednesday, the energy price cap for October onwards will be announced by regulator Ofgem and is expected to hit a three-year high.

A government spokesperson said that in addition to the Warm Homes Discount it was cutting VAT on electricity bills and would do "everything we can" to shield consumers from global energy shocks.

Energy UK chief executive Dhara Vyas said: "Suppliers continue to do all they can to help their customers but as well as persistently high bills, record levels of debt show how the current system is failing to provide the right support to those in need."

A new "social discount" scheme would result in "a system that works better for everyone", she added.

Energy UK says suppliers have a range of support measures for customers, external that includes debt write-off schemes and hardship funds, as well as enhanced funding to charity partners.

However, Adam Scorer, chief executive at National Energy Action (NEA) said: "Heading toward winter with prices spiking again we expect suppliers to do more - listen and respond to their customer who are really struggling.

"More than anything else people need a responsible and empathetic approach to debt," he added.

Ofgem reported at the end of last winter that customers who had fallen behind on their energy bills owed suppliers a record Â£4.7bn. Since then wholesale energy prices have risen, following the start of the Iran war in February.

Energy consultancy Cornwall Insight predicts Ofgem's cap on household price rises, which is set every three months, will go up by 4% when it is announced on Wednesday.

The rise will apply to household bills during the first half of the coming winter and follows a sharper 13% rise in July.

The energy cap covers around 33 million households in England, Wales and Scotland.

It fixes the maximum amount which customers on standard variable tariffs can be charged for each unit of gas and electricity used, but households' actual bills depend on the amount of energy they use and how they pay for it.

News.title: Scammers increasingly using QR codes to steal money and data
News.content:
When Les Howard could not find change for parking during a trip to the coast, a quick response (QR) code on the meter seemed to be the answer.

But the next day, the 61-year-old realised he had become the victim of an increasingly common scam as criminals started taking money from his bank account in Â£60 chunks.

Reports of QR code-related scams have gone up by 700% in the past four years, figures by Report Fraud have revealed.

Experts say criminals are finding different ways to exploit the codes as they become a common part of everyday life.

This could be disguising suspicious links in emails, gaining access to victims' messaging apps or convincing people who are out and about to download fraudulent apps to steal their money and data.

That is what happened to Howard, from Widnes, who was visiting Caernarfon in North Wales with his wife.

"We went to the car park where we normally go," Howard told the BBC Scam Secrets podcast.

"I normally have change in the car to pay for the parking, but this time I didn't.

"So there was a QR code to download and get an app and pay via an app."

News.title: Wicker Man director's sons complete their late father's film trilogy
News.content:
Robin Hardy always envisaged his iconic 1973 folk horror film The Wicker Man as the first part of a trilogy.

The Wicker Tree, released in 2011, brought him closer to that ambition, but his death in 2016 at the age of 86 left the project incomplete.

Now his sons, Justin and Dominic, have been able to complete their father's trilogy, after finding a script for the final film.

Wrath of the Gods has its premiere at the FrightFest horror festival in London, external on Friday, a family dream made possible thanks to the surprise discovery of some long-lost family archive.

"The person who bought Justin's old family home said they'd discovered six sacks of letters, scripts and other material pertaining to Robin Hardy and The Wicker Man in the attic," says Dominic, an art historian at the University of Quebec in Montreal.

"Justin's first instinct was to burn them, but we couldn't ignore this original source material. Although we left it unopened for six months or more."

News.title: Iran-linked hackers behind cyber attack that shut down power plant, reports say
News.content:
A small power plant in the UK was shut down during a cyber attack.

The government said that at no point was there a risk to the UK's energy system, but the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) has contacted power companies to advise them about the risk of cyber attacks.

The Telegraph reported, external that the attack, which took place last month, was carried out by hackers affiliated to the Iranian regime.

For security reasons, neither the government nor the National Cyber Security Centre, which deals with attacks on critical infrastructure, would give further details of the site affected. However this was not an attack on an essential service such as a large power station.

According to the Telegraph, the power plant was shut down for four days.

DESNZ said the incident had affected a small-scale generator and at no point had there been a risk to the wider energy system.

The UK's power network has a number of smaller gas generators which provide short-term power when needed.

Protecting the country's supplies is a key challenge for the government. It is updating its regulations for cyber security, and working on a new energy resilience strategy for later this year.

Iran has long been regarded as a capable cyber power but while the Western cyber-security world is braced for attacks either from the state or hackers linked to the state as a result of its conflict with the US this year, there has been little activity so far.

News.title: 'My skin makes me unique and I'm learning to embrace it'
News.content:
A woman born with a rare genetic skin condition that covers 98% of her body in birthmarks has spoken of how she is learning to embrace her appearance after years of trying to hide it.

Laura Kelly, 28, was born with congenital melanocytic naevus (CMN) and underwent 14 operations as a baby, with doctors fearing she may not live beyond the age of eight.

Laura said CMN made her self conscious about how strangers might react and that, growing up as a teenager, she often wore heavy makeup and planned outfits to cover her skin.

She said embracing how she looks and raising awareness of CMN has given her more confidence and hopes sharing her story will help others with a visible difference.

News.title: Davis 'grateful' for support over cancer diagnosis
News.content:
It was the first time Davis had appeared at a public event since announcing on 11 August that she has stage four breast cancer.

She said in that announcement it had "metastasised" to her bones following a diagnosis a year-and-half-ago, meaning it was "too late" for chemotherapy.

Davis signed autographs and posed for photographs before appearing on Saturday's panel.

Some fans posing questions told the actress "I love you so much", but she was not asked directly about her health.

The Shaun of the Dead director, Edgar Wright, and Simon Pegg, who played the lead role in the cult British movie, were also on the panel. Davis portrayed Dianne, an aspiring actress who was one of the core group of survivors of a zombie apocalypse, and helps Pegg's character Shaun fight off the legions of the undead.

Her favourite memories of filming, she said, were "when we all pretended to be zombies and walked across the square; it was like being naughty schoolkids.

"It was a fun time, we went a bit mad."

The actress, who played receptionist Dawn Tinsley in the BBC sitcom The Office and whose father is comedian Jasper Carrott, was also applauded when asked for advice about getting into the film industry.

She said: "We all grow up with a different life with a different world telling us we all have limitations.

"None of us do, our only limitations are things that we think are limiting. We can do anything, or be anybody, and don't apologise for that."

Davis had thanked fans for their "kindness and support" in another post two days after revealing she had cancer.

"OK, so the last two days have been utterly overwhelming, in that I had zero idea my cancer post would have the attention it did," she said.

"Truly, I am in shock. That said, thank you to everyone for the tremendous amount of kindness and support you have sent me. Good grief it was emotional."

News.title: Baby whose parents feared had just days to live is 'thriving' after life-saving heart operation
News.content:
A baby, whose parents feared had just days to live, is "thriving" after having life-saving operations on his heart.

Macs Green, a previously "completely healthy baby" suffered two cardiac arrests and was diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy - which can lead to heart failure.

After a struggle to find suitable hospital beds, he has now had device called a Berlin Heart, external fitted, which takes over the function of his heart.

He still needs a transplant and doctors have told his parents Catrin and Dylan they do not know how long the wait will be before he gets one.

But, after his operation in Newcastle's Freeman Hospital, Dylan said Macs was already "completely different" from how he was before.

Before surgery he had been in a specialist unit in Bristol Royal Children's Hospital on an extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, external (Ecmo) machine, which helped pump oxygenated blood around his body.

News.title: I'd swell up once a week - now my life has changed
News.content:
"It's changed my life. I can do everything I want to now. It's brilliant," says Jack Cope.

The 30-year-old joiner, from Bedford, has had hereditary angioedema (HAE), a condition which causes severe unpredictable swelling and painful attacks, since birth.

The swelling occurs all over his body, including in his throat, stomach and face. Even something as simple as using a hammer can cause his hand to swell.

But now, due to a trial at Addenbrooke's Hospital, in Cambridge, he is trying a new treatment which he says has massively reduced his symptoms.

"I was having about an attack a week and I've gone from that to nothing for nearly a year now," he says.

News.title: Newcastle vs Liverpool LIVE: Isak faces hostile Premier League return after emotional Kevin Keegan tributes
News.content:
( PA )

Newcastle host Liverpool in the Premier League’s late kick off this afternoon with both clubs having undergone managerial changes in the summer break.

Eddie Howe departed as Newcastle boss following the sales of Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon with his replacement Matthias Jaissle tasked with rebuilding the team this season. He faces a difficult opener with the Magpies winless in their last 19 top-flight encounters with Liverpool, though regime change at Anfield as well could present an opportunity to end that run.

Andoni Iraola takes charge of Liverpool having replaced Arne Slot. He will be hoping to bring the best out of Alexander Isak, who faces a hostile return to St James’ Park, and Florian Wirtz who underperformed in their first season with the Reds while also figuring out how exactly Liverpool can replace Mohamed Salah who has departed for Turkey. Iraola has himself admitted his squad was “thin” in some areas.

It is also set to be an emotional afternoon at St James’ Park as Newcastle and Liverpool join together to pay tribute to Kevin Keegan, who was a legendary figure at both clubs. Keegan passed away in July at the age of 75 and fans of both clubs will pay tribute before kick-off.

Seven people have died, including two police officers, in a “devastating”car crash following a chase in the early hours of Saturday morning.

Police had been chasing a Volkswagen Passat with five male occupants which was suspected of being driven with cloned number plates, but aborted the pursuit after the car started driving the wrong way down the A66 in Southbank, near Middlesbrough.

Ten seconds later, the VW collided with an oncoming Cleveland Police armed response vehicle which was not involved in the pursuit.

The two officers, who died at the scene, have been named as PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38.

Five young men travelling the VW were also killed. They have been named as Makai Saddington, 18, Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Worthy, 16, and Jacob Matusiak, 23.

The police watchdog the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) confirmed it has launched an investigation into the fatal crash.

Below is everything we know about the incident so far.

open image in gallery A police cordon at the scene of a fatal crash involving a police car and a Volkswagen Passat on the A66 in South Bank, near Middlesbrough ( PA )

How did the crash occur?

Cleveland Police launched a pursuit after spotting a Volkswagen Passat which was acting “suspiciously”, the force said in the aftermath of the fatal crash.

Analysis of the police vehicle in-car footage shows the chase lasted just under seven minutes before the Passat travelled onto the A66 against the flow of traffic, at which point the pursuit was aborted, according to the IOPC.

Just 10 seconds later, the Passat collided with another police vehicle which was not involved in the pursuit. It was in the area to assist in a search for the Passat, which was suspected to be using cloned number plates.

Fourteen ambulance crews rushed to the scene, including emergency ambulance crews, a specialist paramedic, a Hazardous Area Response Team and a doctor from Great North Air Ambulance Service. Despite their best efforts, all the occupants were pronounced dead at the scene.

Doorbell footage from nearby Lime Road appears to show multiple police vehicles chasing a car at speed moments before Saturday's fatal crash.

The footage was filmed at 3:36am - three minutes before the Passat collided with the marked police vehicle.

The A66 was closed in both directions between Normanby Road and Church Lane in Eston as a result of the smash as investigators examined the wreckage. A large white tent was erected over the scene, with multiple emergency service vehicles around.

The closed section of the A66 is bordered by large industrial units to the north and is close to the major Teesworks site.

The police watchdog, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), confirmed they had launched an investigation into the “tragic incident” following a mandatory referral from the local force.

In an update on Sunday, IOPC director of engagement Derrick Campbell said: “We have obtained initial accounts of officers involved in the pursuit, the incident log and in car footage of the incident. Work is ongoing to obtain additional material.

“IOPC investigators will continue to review and analyse all the evidence that is available to us. We will not be providing any further comment at this time.”

open image in gallery The police watchdog has launched an investigation into the incident ( PA Wire )

What have police said about the incident?

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was “devastated” to hear of the deaths of two police officers and five members of the public in a crash near Middlesbrough in the early hours of this morning.

Chief Constable Victoria Fuller, of Cleveland Police, said the force would co-operate fully with the investigation as she urged the public not to speculate on the circumstances of the crash.

“This is an incredibly sad day for Cleveland,” she said in an emotional statement delivered outside the force’s Middlesbrough headquarters. “This loss is being felt across our communities, by our police family, and by our partner agencies.

“These were brave officers, protecting our communities and serving our residents. Who didn’t return home to their families at the end of their shift.

“My thoughts, and the thoughts of everyone at Cleveland Police, are with their families, friends, colleagues and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time.

“Earlier today, the Deputy Chief Constable and I visited Matthew and Tom's families to offer our condolences, support one another, and begin to come to terms with this unimaginable loss.”

Cleveland Police Federation chairwoman Lauren Somerville added: “Words cannot describe the pain the Cleveland Police family are feeling today.

“Our colleagues who should have been going home to their loved ones at the end of their shifts are not. And that is just unfathomable.

“Cleveland Police Federation will be offering full support to our fallen colleagues’ families and they have all of our love and care at this time.

“When the time is right we will pay full tribute to our brave colleagues. But we can assure that their sacrifice will never be forgotten.”

What do we know about the victims?

The two police officers killed in the crash have been named as PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38.

Cleveland Police Chief Constable Fuller said: “These were brave officers protecting our communities and serving our residents who didn’t return home to their families at the end of their shift.”

Tributes have also been paid to the five young men travelling in the VW Passat, who were aged between 16 and 23.

Anna Turley, MP for the Redcar constituency where the accident happened, said on Sunday morning the “whole community is reeling”.

She told Sky News: “I want to particularly put on record my tribute to our incredibly brave police officers, PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough, because we know our police officers every day, every night put themselves into action to protect our communities, to keep them safe.

“And I want to acknowledge their bravery, but I also want to recognise that we’ve lost seven lives tragically and the whole community is obviously in shock and devastation.”

Taylor Sheridan has been accused of stealing the idea for Yellowstone from a writer’s 2016 pitch, according to a new copyright infringement lawsuit.

In the complaint, obtained by The Independent, Lauren J. Salkin alleges that her rejected pitch bore a number of striking similarities to Sheridan’s hit neo-Western drama.

101 Studios, Paramount Global and NBCUniversal are also named as defendants in the suit.

The Independent has contacted representatives for Sheridan and those companies for comment.

In the complaint, Salkin’s lawyers claim she spent more than a decade developing a television series named Sovereign Nation, which centered on “tribal governance, casino-driven economic power, and a modern war over land and development.”

open image in gallery Taylor Sheridan is accused of copying the idea for ‘Yellowstone’ from a writer’s 2016 pitch in a new lawsuit ( Getty )

open image in gallery Kevin Costner starred as John Dutton in Sheridan’s wildly successful Western drama ( Paramount )

Salkin claims she submitted Sovereign Nation to Taylor Sheridan’s representatives in late 2016 and received a rejection in February 2017. “Taylor thanks you very much for your interest. Unfortunately, he’s unavailable for TV projects,” read the response from his representatives, according to the suit.

Months later, Yellowstone was greenlit by Paramount and its first episode aired on June 20, 2018.

Yellowstone starred Kevin Costner as ranch patriarch John Dutton and followed his family’s fight to protect their sprawling Montana ranch from developers, Native American tribes and rival interests seeking to seize control of their land.

Yellowstone ran for five wildly successful seasons from 2018 to 2024, shattering cable viewing records and spawning an expansive television franchise.

Salkin’s lawyers claim the show “included specific expressive choices already embodied” in Sovereign Nation.

They allegedly included: “A tribal casino functioning as the institutional center of political and development power; a signature confrontation staged in the tribal chairman’s casino office over expansion beyond reservation boundaries; the use of trust land, the absence of zoning restrictions, and a 99-year lease structure as the concrete mechanism for that expansion; and recurring master-plan imagery deployed to dramatize the struggle for territorial control.”

Furthermore, Salkin’s lawyers also claim that she suggested actors Danny Huston and Gil Birmingham in her pitch deck. Both were later cast in Yellowstone and played “materially parallel structural roles,” they allege: “Birmingham as the tribal political leader whose authority and development strategy run through the casino, and Huston as the outside development power broker who supplies the political or commercial path for that expansion.”

open image in gallery The claimant’s lawyers claim Gil Birmingham (right) was cast in ‘Yellowstone’ months after she suggested the actor for the project she pitched to Sheridan ( Getty )

Sheridan had previously cast Birmingham in his 2017 film Wind River, however.

The suit goes on to claim that a senior, unnamed HBO TV executive who had reviewed materials for Sovereign Nation later told her he recognized similarities in Yellowstone and rejected Sheridan’s show for that reason.

“When the works are objectively compared, the same coordinated design repeatedly appears: casino-centered institutions organize political power; the same unusual land-development mechanisms propel the conflict; parallel scenes perform the same dramatic functions; and the same actors appear in materially parallel roles,” the complaint says.

“These are not merely convergences of a shared genre. Taken together with access and timing, they support a strong inference of copying.”

Salkin is seeking damages and profits tied to alleged copyright infringement and injunctive relief preventing future infringement.

“This is a classic David-versus-Goliath situation,” Salkin’s attorney Paul B. Lackey told The Hollywood Reporter.

“She spent years putting together the specific and multi-layered framework for a story that has become the biggest streaming success of all time. She has watched the vast commercial success of this story that was stolen from her and decided that enough was enough. We will do everything in our power to get her justice.”

A summer of change off the pitch for Aston Villa was followed by one of the worst opening 45 minutes of a season in Premier League history as Unai Emery’s side collapsed at Brighton.

Last season’s Europa League winners went into the new campaign having lost four of the players that started their 3-0 win over Freiburg in May. Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa’s exits could also soon be followed by two more first-team stars in Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez, who were both left out of Villa’s matchday squad at Brighton.

A new-look Villa went behind inside eight minutes in calamitous fashion as Victor Lindelof bundled into his own net before Brighton’s Maxim De Cuyper doubled their advantage. Jack Hinshelwood then scored twice in two minutes before Villa’s Joao Gomes, a £38m signing from Wolves, was sent off on his first Premier League appearance for his new club.

Hinshelwood’s first goal was followed by another straight from kick-off. Gomes was caught in possession on the edge of his own box before Hinshelwood finished into an empty net for his second - just 80 seconds after his first.

It then went from bad to worse for debutant Gomes, who was earlier booked for waving an imaginary yellow card towards Pascal Gross, as he received a straight red card for kicking out at Georginio Rutter.

According to Opta, Gomes became just the second Premier League player to be sent off in the first half of his first appearance for club, after QPR's Samba Diakite in 2012, while Brighton became just the third team to lead by four goals at half-time on the opening weekend in Premier League history.

There were empty seats in the Villa away end before half-time, and the potential for further embarrassment to come, amid a hugely uncertain period for the Europa League winners, although the fans who remained continued to chant Emery’s name.

open image in gallery There were empty seats in the Villa end before half time ( Getty )

open image in gallery Villa fans saw their team fall apart in the first half ( Getty )

Villa have recouped huge fees for their departing stars, receiving a record £117m for Rogers from Chelsea, £51m for England defender Konsa and £35m for Tielemans, but the uncertainty off the field is undoubtedly a concern.

Villa have broken their transfer record to sign Johan Manzambi, who was unavailable due to injury, while Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki appears to be the replacement for Martinez but was only ready to be named on the bench.

Alejandro Garnacho and Aaron Wan-Bissaka have arrived on loan and Matteo Ruggeri has been signed as Emery attempts to rebuild his side. They have also been linked with a move for Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson.

“I’m very excited, I think we have had an intelligent market,” Emery said on Friday. “We know where we are and we know what we want to do again for the next year. This is the priority and this is the motivation I have.”

Villa striker Watkins is wanted by Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, and his omission from the travelling squad to the south coast will only heighten speculation that the England international is set to join the exodus.

Manager Emery provided a bizarre response when asked if this omission signalled the end for Watkins’ time at Villa, taking a lengthy pause before replying: "Silence." Emery previously said in a press conference that he wants to keep Watkins but has already confirmed that bids have been made for the 30-year-old.

Next up for Villa is a home match against Premier League champions Arsenal on Monday.

Natalie Harp, the president’s close aide who has been the subject of recent intense speculation, was spotted with Trump on another golf course this weekend.

The 35-year-old aide and the president, along with other staffers, were pictured at Trump National in Sterling, Virginia, Saturday. Harp, wearing golf attire, was seen carrying several devices including a laptop, as well as a branded “Trump” bag. As they left the golf course, Trump entered an SUV on the passenger side and then Harp also jumped in the backseat, according to the White House pool report.

The president remained in the D.C. area this weekend as he is set to wave the flag at the Indy 250 Grand Prix event - which will see drivers race a 1.7-mile circuit in the heart of the capital - Sunday. Trump is also expected to take a lap of the official course in the presidential motorcade.

Harp has been thrust into the national spotlight after her close relationship with the president was called out by Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff during a campaign rally in Georgia last weekend as he claimed that the president was distracted from the ongoing Iran war and resulting economic crisis by petty issues like his D.C. beautification projects.

“He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie,” Ossoff said.

open image in gallery Natalie Harp is seen among the president's staffers at his golf club in Sterling, Virginia, on Saturday ( Getty )

open image in gallery Harp rides in an SUV carrying Trump as they leave Trump National Golf Club ( Getty )

Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive Democrat running for Senate in Michigan, was the latest opposition lawmaker to make remarks as the scrutiny over Harp’s role grows.

Responding Saturday to a clip of Trump attacking him, El-Sayed directed a public message at Harp: “Natalie, I think he’s had a little too much iPad for the week. He needs his rest.”

Harp is known as the “Human Printer”, according to reports, because her role involves carrying a portable printer in order to present Trump with hard copies of positive news stories and statements from people praising him.

Reports have also revealed how Harp often leaves effusive and extremely personal notes for the president, to extent that her activity even alarmed Secret Service agents. Her estranged brother has called her relationship with Trump “unhealthy” in interviews.

open image in gallery Natalie Harp and White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt trail the president at Joint Base Andrews as he heads to a campaign rally in South Carolina Friday ( AFP/Getty )

One of those notes, reported earlier this week, related to another golf trip. After Harp sprinted after the president’s golf cart during a May 2023 visit to his course in Aberdeen, Scotland, she wrote a note to Trump apologizing for the spectacle.

"I also am sorry if I was an embarrassment walking the course in Scotland ... I want things to always be right between us. I also know I've been distracted all week (forgetting to eat throughout the days, and even forgetting to sleep, and only catching a couple hours at a time),” she wrote, according to reports.

On Saturday, CNN revealed scores of posts Harp made on X before her account was suspended.

The posts repeatedly urged Trump’s supporters on January 6 to "FIGHT FOR TRUMP!". The posts also addressed Trump directly, telling the outgoing president, “We love you.”

open image in gallery Harp is rarely absent from the president’s side during domestic or foreign trips ( AFP/Getty )

The attention on Harp has elicited furious responses from White House aides and senior MAGA world figures.

The president’s top defender on CNN, Scott Jennings, issued a passionate defense of Harp on social media and in TV appearances this past week.

White House communications director Steven Cheung issued an acidic attack against Ossoff. “Jon Jackoff has to be the biggest cuck loser in politics,” wrote the White House communications director.

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

News.title: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions
News.content:
The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

News.title: George Russell king of the sprint and driving with freedom after engagement
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix, the first race after F1’s summer break. Kimi Antonelli has had a tremendous first part of the season, leading Lewis Hamilton by 50 points and George Russell by 59 after the first 11 rounds. He has taken six wins to Russell’s two, with Hamilton, Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc all racking up a win apiece.

His start to the second part of the season was not the best, however. A messy sprint qualifying session meant he ended down in fifth, more than 0.2sec behind team-mate Russell, who took a much-needed pole.

Some of the damage was self-inflicted, quite literally. In the first session of sprint qualifying he ran wide at the banked turn 12 and into the gravel. The damage to the floor of his car was attempted to be repaired for the rest of the session but left him lacking downforce. A gap of 0.2sec is not enormous but the other issue was that three other cars – Norris, Leclerc and Piastri – are between him and Russell.

That said, it is not a great worry at this point. The points available in the sprint are relatively small and Antonelli has a healthy margin at this point over his rivals. In any case, there is no guarantee that Russell and Antonelli finish where they will start. Antonelli has shown on numerous occasions that he can bounce back from a difficult session and you have to expect that again here.

The race, which starts at 11am BST, is one-third of the race distance and should be run in dry conditions. There have been persistent showers and a steady breeze at Zandvoort this weekend, but it is not expected to affect the running in the sprint.

Qualifying for tomorrow’s grand prix comes later today at 3pm, which could be a more consequential session.

News.title: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

Full team news as and when we get it.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

Sports.title: Alejandro Balde ‘excited by Man Utd transfer’ but Red Devils face battle to land Barcelona left-back
Sports.content:
ALEJANDRO BALDE is “excited” by the prospect of signing for Manchester United before the transfer deadline.

But the Red Devils face a battle to agree a fee with Barcelona.



Balde, 22, is a product of Barca’s academy but could depart amid competition at left-back from Gerard Martin and new signing Joao Cancelo.

According to Spanish outlet Sport, Balde has approved a potential transfer to agent Jorge Mendes.



Among the Spain international’s options, United are said to be the suitor that “excites” him most.

Michael Carrick‘s side are keen to sign a new left-back.



Lewis Hall is a long-term target, but a deal is not easy to do.

And the Red Devils have also been linked with Arsenal academy graduate Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Barca could approve a Balde sale in a bid to raise funds.

Club chiefs are said to have valued him at as much as £38million, but it remains to be seen at which number they would sell to United.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Balde recently addressed his future, saying: “The team is in good shape, it’s been a different pre-season because the World Cup players have come back afterwards.

“The team is fine, physically, very well.”

Balde made 42 appearances in all competitions last season, including 28 in LaLiga.

In total he has played 168 times for his boyhood club since graduating from La Masia.

The hometown hero has already won three LaLiga titles and a Copa del Rey during his stint in the first team.



Barca are set to kick off their LaLiga campaign against Elche this evening.

Balde has NOT been included in the matchday squad, amid speculation about his future.

Team-mates Marc Casado and Hector Fort have also been excluded as they face potential exits.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Man Utd, meanwhile, started with veteran Luke Shaw at left-back in their 2-0 defeat at Hull on Saturday.

Patrick Dorgu is seen as more of an attacking option, while Noussair Mazraoui is more comfortable on the right.

Sports.title: Aston Villa concede FOUR in just 30 minutes vs Brighton as new-look side capitulate after they are ‘decimated by PSR’
Sports.content:
ASTON VILLA suffered a nightmare start to the Premier League season after conceding FOUR goals in their opening 30 minutes.

Unai Emery’s side are looking to build on their fourth-place finish from last season.



But they were in for a rude awakening on their return to Prem football as they were dismantled almost immediately by Fabian Hurzeler’s Brighton.

It took the seagulls just eight minutes to break through thanks to Victor Lindelof’s calamitous own goal.



Maxim De Cuyper added a second 10 minutes later to put the hosts in control.

And Jack Hinshelwood put the home fans in dreamland as he added two more goals in as many minutes to make it 4-0.



The latter of those goals came as the Brighton academy graduate capitalised on a loose bit of play from Prem debutant Joao Gomes to steal the ball in the box and tuck an effort home.

And if that wasn’t already a rough start to life in his new colours, he was sent off in the 40th minute to compound Emery’s issues.

The Brazilian midfielder was deemed to have kicked out at an opposition player from the floor after a brief VAR check.

He was then given his marching orders, huffing as he exited the field just 40 minutes into one of the worst Prem debuts on record.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Fans could not believe their eyes, with one writing: “I worry for Aston Villa. Brilliant English club decimated by PSR.”

Another added: “Will Villa fans blame this on how unfairly they’ve been pillaged by rivals in the transfer market?”

Sports.title: Marc Guehi handed shock new position for Man City in Enzo Maresca’s first game in charge against Bournemouth
Sports.content:
ENZO MARESCA sprung a huge surprise in his opening Premier League showdown in charge of Manchester City – after handing Marc Guehi a start in midfield.

The Italian tactician, 46, was appointed as the title challengers’ new boss following Pep Guardiola’s exit at the end of last season.



And, having suffered a thumping 3-0 defeat to Arsenal in the Community Shield, Maresca made a shock decision to move Guehi away from his usual role.

The centre-back was shifted into the heart of the midfield as City looked to get their Premier League campaign off to a winning start against Bournemouth.



Guehi partnered Elliot Anderson, who headed to the Etihad Stadium in a club-record £116million deal during the summer, in the middle of the park.

Ruben Dias and Abdukodir Khusanov were given the nod in his favoured position.

Maresca turned to Guehi, 26, after Rodri’s exit was confirmed earlier this month.

The Spaniard’s move to reigning LaLiga champions Barcelona has left City short of defensive midfield options.

Bernardo Silva quit the Etihad Stadium when his contract expired at the end of last season.

Kalvin Phillips was also allowed to join Sheffield United on loan after struggling to make his mark at City.

Sports.title: Dan Burn out for weeks with ankle injury – just days after Newcastle star was slammed by fans over wedding spin video
Sports.content:
BURNT OUT Dan Burn out for weeks with ankle injury – just days after Newcastle star was slammed by fans over wedding spin video

NEWCASTLE captain Dan Burn is set to miss the next few weeks with an ankle injury, according to Sky Sports.

The huge defender suffered the injury in training, just days after he caused controversy with a wedding stunt.



The news came ahead of Newcastle‘s Premier League opener at home to Liverpool.

It’s a huge blow for new Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle, who could be without his captain for a while.



The news also comes just days after the Geordie was slammed by fans after a video emerged of him being spun around at a wedding.

Following this, one fan wrote: “Paper thin squad and you’ve got Dan Burn pulling stunts like this a week before the season starts.”

It’s understand the injury is not related to the wedding, but due to him rolling his ankle in training.

It’s also been reported that he’s wearing a protective boot to limit movement.

Burn was named Newcastle skipper last week, following Bruno Guimaraes’ switch to Prem champions Arsenal.

Jaissle has clearly placed a lot of trust in the England star, who looks to be out for at least the opening two games.

Today’s Super Sunday clash at 4:30 is expected to see former Toon hero Alexander Isak return to St James’ Park for the first time since his big-money move last summer.

New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola will be hoping to get a tune out of the Swede after an injury-ridden first campaign in red.

Sports.title: Arsenal in talks with Al Hilal over Gabriel Martinelli transfer which would see Gunners make highest-ever sale
Sports.content:
GABRIEL MARTINELLI is open to a stunning move to Saudi Arabia with Al-Hilal reportedly in talks with Arsenal over a £60million deal for the winger.

The Saudi Pro League giants have opened negotiations with the Gunners over a move for the Brazil international.



No agreement has yet been reached between the clubs, with negotiations also ongoing with Martinelli’s camp.

But the 25-year-old is open to the possibility of joining Al-Hilal, according to The Athletic’s David Ornstein.



A deal anywhere near Arsenal’s £60million asking price would smash their outgoing transfer record, which has stood since Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain joined Liverpool for £35m in 2017.

Arsenal are understood to be happy with a £60m fee to allow Martinelli to leave the Emirates.

It comes after the attacker turned down the chance to move to Turkey amid interest from Galatasaray.

Martinelli’s position at Arsenal has become increasingly precarious after being left out of the squad for both the Community Shield.

He was also absent for the Gunners’ opening Premier League 3-0 victory against Coventry City.

The Brazilian has been at Arsenal since arriving from Ituano in 2019 and has gone on to become a key figure under Mikel Arteta.

He has scored 62 goals in 278 appearances for the club, helping Arsenal challenge for major honours during his seven years in England.

But Martinelli is now entering the final year of his current contract, although Arsenal hold an option to extend his stay for another season.

And Al-Hilal’s move could now hand Arsenal the chance to bank a huge fee for the winger before the transfer window slams shut.

Sports.title: Best reactions to Haaland’s shock new haircut as Noel Gallagher, Pep, Zlatan and his girlfriend give mixed verdict
Sports.content:
ERLING HAALAND stunned the football world by chopping off his mane of blond hair on Saturday.

The Manchester City striker, 26, had become synonymous with his long flowing locks throughout his four-year stint in the Premier League.



On the eve of the new season, however, Haaland decided to get a dramatic haircut.

After having a trim on Saturday, the Norwegian video-called some of his famous pals to get their live reaction – with the results being uploaded on his YouTube channel.



First up, Haaland gave Oasis superstar and City megafan Noel Gallagher a ring.

The musician, 59, said: “No way mate! When’d you get that done?”



“You look about 17-years-old! It’s good mate, change is good!”

Haaland then phoned City team-mate Jack Grealish.



Laughing, the former England ace said: “You look about 10-years-old! Oh my… that is hilarious!

“I actually can’t stop looking at the front of your head I swear. I love it. See you later brother.”

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Haaland then dared to phone Zlatan Ibrahimovic, a fellow forward that wore his hair long for most of his career.

Pulling no punches, the Swede harshly asked: “What the f*** did you do?

“Oh my god, what the f*** is this? You lost a bet or what? Oh my god – block me and erase my number!



“My wife says you’re crazy. I will be honest with you, I’m always honest. You’re going to be faster now, or what?”

Haaland called his dad Alf-Inge, who joked: “At least you look like me again, yeah?”

And next up was former City boss Pep Guardiola, who answered in bed.



Newly-unemployed Guardiola said: “No way! You’re lucky you have hair! I would love to have!”

Asked if he’s watching football, Pep added: “I’m reading a little bit and watching Brentford-Tottenham.”

Further quizzed if he likes Haaland’s new haircut, Guardiola said: “Yeah, it’s okay. Listen, if you don’t like it, it will grow up. So don’t worry. I love you!”

In addition to YouTube, Haaland also posted his new trim to Instagram.



His post received almost four million likes in barely two hours, with his former Borussia Dortmund team-mate Jude Bellingham commenting: “No way”.

Haaland also had a live reaction to his haircut from girlfriend Isabel Haugseng Johansen.

After looking stunned, Isabel was asked what she thinks by Haaland.

She replied: “You look cute!”



As Haaland jokingly bristled, Isabel added: “I think you look really tough! You look really tough.

“I’ll wake up in the morning and be like ‘who’s that?'”

Fans didn’t have to wait long to see Haaland debut his new barnet on the pitch.

The City striker was handed a start as his side opened their Prem campaign by hosting Bournemouth at the Etihad.

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins OUT of Aston Villa squad to face Brighton as talks continue over shock Al Hilal transfer
Sports.content:
OLLIE WATKINS has been left out of Aston Villa’s matchday squad for the showdown against Brighton – after being heavily linked with a shock exit.

The striker, 30, missed the Midlands giants’ Super Cup loss to Paris Saint-Germain last week.



And Watkins was not part of the travelling party to the south coast after finding himself at the centre of transfer talks.

Al-Hilal are looking to seal a deal which would see the former Brentford man become the latest Premier League star to cash in on the riches on offer in Saudi Arabia.



Uncertainty over Watkins’ future resulted in Villa chief Unai Emery choosing to rule him out of the clash with Brighton.

Emiliano Buendia was deployed as a false No9 for the opening contest of the domestic campaign.



Emery refused to be drawn on Watkins’ future when he was quizzed about his absence during pre-match media duties.

He said: “Silence. We have the players we have today, here. It’s okay. We’re not speaking about it.”

Al-Hilal tested the waters by launching a £38.5million bid for Watkins earlier this week.

And Villa have been scouring the market for potential replacements as the transfer deadline edges closer.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Emery has been tipped to push for Nicolas Jackson, who is out of favour at Chelsea, if Watkins is given the green light to quit.

But the Spanish tactician has been left with limited attacking options while talks over a move away from Villa Park continue.

Watkins played a key role in Villa ending their wait for silverware by winning the Europa League last season.

The marksman notched five goals in the competition, alongside 16 strikes in the top-flight.

And Watkins, who bagged a place in England’s 26-man squad for the World Cup, has found the net 108 times in 278 appearances for Villa.



Emery has already seen a host of key men leave since adding to the trophy cabinet.

Ezri Konsa became the latest big-name departure when he completed a £55m move to Arsenal on Friday.

Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans have also headed through the exit door, joining Chelsea and Manchester United respectively.

Sports.title: Price double gives West Brom turnaround win over Burnley
Sports.content:
Isaac Price inspired West Bromwich Albion to a 3-1 comeback win against promotion favourites Burnley in the Sky Bet Championship.

The Northern Ireland international scored twice in the second half at The Hawthorns after setting up Harry Whitwell's equaliser to cancel out Callum Styles' own goal.

Burnley, without star striker Zian Flemming with an injury amid interest from Lille, failed to match their lofty billing in a disappointing second-half display.

Albion continued their 100 per cent start to the season, gaining their third straight win in all competitions and second in the league to lie second in the early table behind Millwall on goal difference.

But Burnley suffered their first defeat of the campaign as new boss Nicky Hayen still awaits his first Championship win.

How West Brom maintained perfect start

Image: Isaac Price hit a double in West Brom's win

In a fast and furious start, there were two goals in the first 18 minutes.

Styles put into his own net in the eighth minute from Jacob Bruun Larsen's cross. Albion complained that Hannibal Mejbri fouled Felix Horn Myhre in the build-up some 70 yards away, with several passages of play unfolding before the goal.

Whitwell equalised in the 18th minute when he slotted home low to Max Weiss' left from 12 yards for the 20-year-old's first Albion league goal.

But it was Burnley who went closest to scoring again when Bruun Larsen sidefooted against the foot of the post from Marcus Edwards' searching cross.

It was a different story after the break. Inspired by Price, Albion produced a dominant second-half performance, with the perfect start.

Price put them ahead for the first time, in the 46th minute, curling the ball beyond Weiss, who had strayed five yards off his line, into the far corner.

Burnley made a triple change in the 57th minute with the arrival of Ugo Raghouber, Zeki Amdouni, and Dastan Satpayev.

Instead, it was Albion who struck next to effectively seal it, after Bashir Humphreys upended Whitwell for a clear penalty.

Price made no mistake from the spot, firing low to Weiss's right with the 'keeper going the wrong way.

Sports.title: Lopez takes Romero's WBA title to become three-weight champion
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez beat Rolly Romero in Las Vegas on Saturday night to capture the WBA welterweight title and become a three-division world champion.

In his welterweight debut, Lopez secured a majority decision over his friend and sparring partner at the T-Mobile Arena. One judge scored the bout 114-114, while the other two had it 115-113 and 116-112 for Lopez.

It was an impressive return to form from Lopez after his loss to Shakur Stevenson in their WBO super lightweight title fight in January.

"I need to tell you guys, if you lose and you come back, then you never lost because you're a winner," Lopez said afterwards. "I'm a winner. I'm a true example of what winning is, and it ain't about losing. It's about never giving up."

In what was Romero's first appearance since taking the WBA title in an upset decision over Ryan Garcia in May 2025, he landed just 73 of 352 punches thrown, according to Compubox. Lopez landed 124 of 530 total punches.

"I got hit with two punches the whole fight that barely grazed me," said an outraged Romero after suffering his first loss since an eighth-round defeat to Isaac Cruz in March 2024. "I was never in any trouble. When I heard 114-114, I knew it was a robbery."

Romero knocked Lopez off-balance with a counter left hook in the fourth round and had him visibly hurt with a right hand in the fifth, but Lopez recovered quickly and responded with some of his best work in the sixth and seventh rounds.

"I expected something similar to this, just a little more combinations from [him]," said Lopez, who sparred with Romero multiple times in his amateur and early-professional career.

"There was a shot he hit me with that woke me up, and I told him, 'You got to do better than that.' I just kept saying, 'You ain't going to take me out. It's not that easy.'"

The 29-year-old has plenty of potential options in his new division, including WBO champion Devin Haney, the winner of next month's WBC clash between Garcia and Conor Benn, and IBF champion Liam Paro.

The current WBA mandatory challenger is Jack Catterall.

Sports.title: Man City agree record-breaking deal with Lille to sign Bouaddi
Sports.content:
Manchester City have agreed a deal with Lille for Morocco international midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi worth up to £86m (€100m).

City are paying a fixed fee of £81.3m plus £4.3m in add-ons.

The 18-year-old is set to become the most expensive teenage signing in Premier League history, surpassing the £58.9m Manchester United committed to paying Lille for Leny Yoro in 2024.

Lille have secured the fee they were holding out for in negotiations for Bouaddi, who was one of the breakout stars of this summer's World Cup with Morocco.

City are working to rebuild their midfield after the departures of Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders.

For Sunday's game with Bournemouth, Marc Guehi started in the centre of midfield.

They are also interested in Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez and Roma's Manu Kone as potential options to further bolster midfield amid uncertainty over Newcastle target Nico Gonzalez's future.

Bouaddi's arrival will follow City's record-breaking £116m deal to sign Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest earlier in the window.

The teenager is capable of operating as a defensive midfielder or in a more advanced role, giving City further versatility in midfield.

Image: Bouaddi is on the brink of a move to Man City

Those who followed Morocco's recent World Cup campaign will recognise the name Ayyoub Bouaddi. Perhaps those who only took a passing glance will remember him, too. He tends to stand out.

Aside from his throwback curly mop of hair, the way he dominated the big stage with effortless grace over the summer got people talking. The midfielder excelled in his fledgling role at his first major international tournament, particularly noticeable in a group-stage bout with Brazil.

But this was not the first time Carlo Ancelotti found himself ruminating over an opposition player who was "better in the duels" than his own.

Ancelotti's Brazilian midfield was composed of the experienced Casemiro and Bruno Guimaraes, and yet somehow it was Bouaddi that beamed brightest. It struck a familiar chord...
