Yet none can deny that the projects were successfully implemented and moved Nigeria’s development stride forward. It has been admitted that Babangida carried out most of these projects at a time when international oil prices hovered between $9 and $12 a barrel.

Beyond domestic policy, under Babangida’s leadership, Nigeria’s foreign policy assumed a more activist and Afrocentric complexion. For the first time, Nigeria projected its regional power to stabilize the West Africa sub region with military interventions to end bloody civil wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone. Nigeria’s leadership under the famous ECOMOG initiative was globally credited with restoring peace, stability and democracy to both countries.

Key sectors of the populace were obviously marginalized. Women were sidelined. Therefore the administration adopted a conscious gender sensitive posture. The administration was gender sensitive, recognizing the past neglect of women and the need to empower them. The plight of women received robust attention through the Office of the First Lady. Mrs. Maryam Babangida actively pursued a policy of Better Life for Rural Women which sought to empower rural and underprivileged women in general through economic and agro-based empowered programmes.

As a conscious policy, the government introduced several poverty alleviation programmes and institutionalized them. These included the creation of a Peoples Bank and a Community Bank both designed to give access to the poor to credit facilities. Babangida constantly tasked his team to seek ways of mitigating the inequality that was increasing in the society. In spite of embracing a free market system, Babangida believed that it was the responsibility of a compassionate government to give capitalism a “human face” by mitigating the alienating effects of market competition.

The introduction of a market economy alienated many. Vested interests in the old government dominated economy activated the opposition of vested interest to the military government. Also, the imposition of a two –party political system meant the opposition of a political class long used to a multi -party culture. Social unrest and mass discontent fueled political opposition. Occasional riots, demonstrations, labour unrest sent a clear message on the need for the state to don a more compassionate face.

An atmosphere of unrest and turmoil gave Babangida’s reform agenda a bad public image. Student protests, endless labour strikes and general unrest were convenient hiding grounds for a largely political revolt against military rule in general.

These were joined by multipronged schemes by the officer corps of a politicized military who were intent on toppling Babangida to have their turn in power. Harassed and tormented by soldiers and political leaders alike, Babangida balked under pressure to nullify the transition presidential election of June 12, 1993. This was the tragic end of an illustrious reform agenda in the history of Nigeria.

This troublesome ending has left Babangida in Nigeria’s leadership history as perhaps a leader more sinned against than sinning. Over three decades after he left office, Babangida has turned into Nigeria’s most popular former leader from social media reactions to his events, recollections and birthdays.

World.title: Preliminary Observations on Adeleke’s Re-election
World.content:
Let me instantly confess that I was delighted Senator Ademola Adeleke won the August 15, 2026 governorship election in Osun state. The Accord candidate outscored Chief Bola Oyebamiji of the All Progressives Congress (APC) by 511,067 votes to 444,815, coasting home with a margin of 66,252. Dr Najeem Salam of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) came a distant third with 17,180 votes, leading to insinuations that his party folded for Accord to stop the APC. Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola, the ADC leader in the state, would rather eat grass than see the APC reclaim the governorship. But many in the APC would rather take Salam’s tally as core evidence that Aregbesola is a political lightweight.

Why was I delighted Adeleke won? One, I believe in a competitive democracy with multiple choice. The APC already controls 31 of the 36 states. The entire north, minus Bauchi, is APC. The entire south, minus Anambra, Abia, Oyo and Osun, is APC. At this rate, the whole country would be painted in APC colours. I stopped watching the German league because Bayern Munich were always sure to win it. The Scottish league is all about Celtic. For me, there is no joy watching a one-sided affair. APC members and supporters are not complaining though. They would be glad to have all the states in their party. The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) was in that mode until the tables turned in 2015.

Two, I was completely irritated by APC’s impunity prior to the election. They were walking on people’s heads. They let it be known that they would do anything, foul or fair, to uproot Adeleke. Accord leaders were arrested and detained by the police a few weeks before the election. Alhaji Teslim Igbalaye, secretary to the state government (SSG), was arrested for “vote buying”. That was a new one to me. How do you prove vote buying two weeks before voting? Wonderful. One of Osun state’s bank accounts was also frozen by the EFCC. If the APC is subjected to similar scrutiny during elections, many of us would not complain. But why is the opposition the only one on the radar?

Three, without prejudice to his performance as governor, I am happy that Adeleke has refused to tone down his dancing to please his critics. I love it when people are comfortable in their own skins in an age when people-pleasing is the in-thing. A lot of people have lost themselves trying to please the crowd. Social media has become the death of many young people who are body-shamed and bullied. People have to pretend to be what they are not and try to paint a fake picture of themselves just to belong. Adeleke is real. He does not care a hoot. He has been derided for his dancing for years but he keeps moving his feet and body. For all you care, he is burning more calories than his critics.

That said, I have also observed with amusement some conversations around the election. I saw read many comments that made me ask the question: “Why are we like this in this country?” If you believe all that you read, the Osun governorship was a battle between good and evil, hawks and doves, saints and sinners — with Accord being the light and the APC being the darkness. All the violence and vote buying were perpetrated by only the APC, while Accord was squeaky clean — according to the WhatsApp narratives. “APC brought money, people collected it and voted for their conscience.” Those on the ground know that both parties engaged in vote buying and violence.

After he was declared winner, Adeleke re-affirmed his endorsement of President Bola Tinubu of the APC for a second term in office. Anger erupted elsewhere. They said Adeleke had betrayed “the Nigerian masses” who voted for him as a sign of protest against “economic hardship” in the land. From the videos I saw on Twitter (that’s what I still call it), most of those complaining were obviously not from Osun and did not vote in the governorship election. I was wondering why they were crying more than the bereaved. If the “suffering masses” opt to vote for the man that “inflicted economic hardship” on them, how is that my problem? Who has headache, who is swallowing paracetamol?

Many people still don’t want to agree that politics, as the maxim goes, is local. A state can vote PDP in a governorship election and APC in presidential. A zone can vote APC in senatorial and PDP in governorship. There are many things in the mix when it comes to electoral politics: partisanship, primordial sentiments, war chest, etc. Sometimes, people vote by default setting: “My own is my own”. A Yoruba proverb says you can’t have a daughter with a shapely waist and choose to put beads on the waist of another person’s daughter. A random study of Nigeria’s electoral history — even as recent as 2023 — will show that voters can indeed choose different parties for different offices.

But this begs the question: will Osun voters actually support the APC in the 2027 presidential election? Nobody can say for sure. Osun politics has consistently been one of the most competitive in Nigeria in many election cycles. In 2019, APC’s Muhammadu Buhari, a sitting president, defeated PDP’s Atiku Abubakar by 347,634 to 337,377 votes — a margin of just 10,000 votes. It got more interesting in 2023 as Atiku defeated Tinubu, supposedly the homeboy, by 354,336 to 343,945. The 10,000-vote gap does not tell the whole story — Atiku, with the full backing of Adeleke (then of the PDP), won in 20 of the 30 LGAs. Adeleke proved to the APC that he was the biggest politician in Osun.

We can even go as far back as 2015. Buhari defeated PDP’s Goodluck Jonathan by 383,603 to 249,929. That was not a walkover. In 2011, Osun was the only state in southern Nigeria that Jonathan did not win. He would have equalled President Olusegun Obasanjo’s feat of winning the 17 southern states in 2003. No other candidate has recorded that sweeping regional victory in our history, north or south. Jonathan’s failure in Osun in 2011 was attributed to Aregbesola, who had become governor via an election petition. The PDP had been deriding him as a court-made governor, so he wanted to prove to them that he was actually on the ground. But can Aregbesola prove another point in 2027?

In the last three governorship elections, Adeleke has more than shown that he has the strongest support base in the state. In 2018, Chief Adegboyega Oyetola was declared winner by a margin of 482 votes. The rumour in town was that Adeleke had indeed won by 6,000 votes but APC strategists found a way of getting INEC to cancel some results and declare the election inconclusive. The APC did a deal with Senator Iyiola Omisore, then of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), got the EFCC off his back and his seized passport was returned to him. That clearly deal gave Oyetola the edge in the supplementary election. Adeleke can claim to have won the 2018, 2022 and 2026 elections.

Ironically, the brains behind the 2018 magic have now fallen out with the APC hierarchy and have found themselves in political wilderness, although some of them have nestled in the ADC. The long and short of it, therefore, is that the Osun electorate (not “electorates”, as Nigerian grammar) can be said to have a mind of its own. Assuming that the voters would opt for Tinubu in 2027 is sort of a gamble, even though conventional wisdom suggests that the election might follow primordial — rather than partisan — lines. There were over one million votes in the state governorship election and Osun is a classic swing state. That massive vote bank must look very alluring to Tinubu and Atiku.

My final observation, or question, for now is: where did Tinubu really stand on Adeleke? On the surface, he looked neutral, having ordered the EFCC to unfreeze the state’s account. Chief Nyesom Wike, the FCT minister, also said the president would have sent him to Osun if he really wanted to win. It appears Wike sees himself as omnipotent — an attribute we usually reserve for God. But the deployment of soldiers to Osun for the election — something only the commander-in-chief can do — and the way they intimidated Accord supporters would tend to contradict the neutrality claim. I am genuinely lost on how neutral Tinubu was, but Adeleke appears fully pleased. That should settle it.

AND FOUR OTHER THINGS…

VOTE SUBSIDY

Alhaji Atiku Abubakar dropped a banger on Thursday: he will restore petrol subsidy if he is elected president next year. This should resonate well with ordinary voters who can point to higher petrol prices as the reason for the rising cost of living. Atiku used to classify subsidy as fraud but now says it is the removal that is a fraud. Confused? Don’t be: the ADC presidential candidate wants to win an election and what better way to connect with the grassroots than to make this earthshaking promise even if he does not intend to restore the subsidy? If I were Atiku, I would further promise to make $1 equal to N1. That is what millions of people want to hear and it will surely win plenty votes. Politics.

UNCENSORED CENSUS

Dr Paul Enenche, senior pastor of Dunamis International Gospel Centre, has called for a census to determine the number of Christians and Muslims in Nigeria. He was reacting to comments by Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir, the Islamic cleric who said Muslims would use their numbers to re-elect a Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket. Incidentally, religion was removed from the census questionnaire in 1992 because of Nigeria’s religious tension. Ethnicity was omitted in 2006 because of the supremacy battle among the country’s biggest ethnic groups. I don’t know what big purpose religion will serve but I support Enenche’s proposal as long as no one will reject the outcome if it doesn’t favour them. Deal?

NAIRA RAIN

The three tiers of government shared N3.007 trillion for July 2026 — the highest ever in nominal terms. This was about N500 billion more than the June share. The federal government got N1.14 trillion while states and LGAs received N943.35 billion and N673.64 billion respectively. Oil-producing states shared an additional N243.47 billion as 13 percent derivation. So what? This would be good news if it translates to more paved roads, more hospital beds, equipment and drugs, more libraries and laboratories in secondary schools, and more clean water. It is the duty of every citizen to put the leaders under pressure to deliver the goods. Action!

NO COMMENT

The speed with which the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) sacked the technical crew of the Super Falcons after Nigeria failed to win WAFCON and were eliminated from the 2027 Women’s World Cup was fishy and alarming. The NFF also quickly set up a “fact-finding committee” made up entirely of football people without an independent management expert to act as a third eye. What is fact finding? What facts are they going to find? The Super Eagles failed to qualify for two FIFA World Cups in a row and the Golden Eaglets last played at the U-17 World Cup in 2019. Just when you thought it was the NFF itself that should be sacked, the subject has turned itself to the predicate. Hahahaha…

World.title: Tinubu Asks APC Campaign Council to Defeat Forces Seeking to Take Nigeria Backwards
World.content:
*President heads campaign council; Yari emerges as DG, accepts appointment

*Shettima, Yilwatda named vice chairmen; Uzodimma secretary

*ADC: APC campaign council a rehabilitation centre for corruption suspects

Deji Elumoye and Chuks Okocha in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu yesterday charged the members of the high-powered Presidential Campaign Council of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the January 2027 presidential election to defeat all those forces who planned to take Nigeria backwards.

The ruling APC yesterday announced the constitution of the campaign council with President Tinubu as Chairman.



At the same time, former Governor of Zamfara State and serving Senator, Abdulaziz Yari and Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State emerged as the Director-General and Secretary, respectively.

According to a statement issued by presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, Vice President Kashim Shettima will serve as vice chairman of the council.



The party’s Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, will also serve as vice chairman; APC National Secretary, Senator Ajibola Bashiru and Special Adviser to the President, Hadiza Bala-Usman, will serve as deputy and assistant secretaries.

Meanwhile, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has described the APC campaign council as a “rehabilitation centre” for persons facing unresolved corruption questions.



Tinubu charged all council members to work tirelessly to deliver victory for the party in the January 2027 elections.

He has also encouraged the leaders of the various directorates to reach out to other party members who may not have been formally listed to join their crucial efforts.



“We have delivered on our campaign promises and set our country on a path of economic progress. We are definitely out of the dark tunnel and are now at the cusp of reaping the benefits of a prosperous economy that will benefit all Nigerians. As we march into the campaign season, we have many achievements to trumpet—let us confidently showcase our record and inspire hope in every corner of our nation. Let us soundly defeat all those forces who plan to take our country backwards,” explained.



According to the statement by Onanuga, President Tinubu, as chairman of the council, will work with a body of advisers, namely: Pioneer National Chairman of the APC, Chief Bisi Akande; former Ogun State Governor, Chief Segun Osoba; ex-Imo State Governor, Senator Rochas Okorocha; former national chairman of APC, Senator Abdullahi Adamu; and former presidential aide, Senator Florence Ita Giwa.



The statement disclosed that the Senate President, Senator Godswill Akpabio; the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Tajudeen Abass; and Governor Mai Mala Buni of Yobe State have been appointed as deputy directors-general for the campaign in the south and the north, respectively.



The statement noted that they would work with the Senate Leader, Senator Bamidele Opeyemi and Deputy Senate President, Senator Jibril Barau, in the two zones.

Continuing, the statement explained that the former National Chairman of the APC, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, would serve as deputy director-general in charge of mobilisation.



In contrast, the President’s Chief of Staff, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, will serve as deputy director-general for administration.

The statement added that a member of the House of Representatives, Hon. James Abiodun Faleke, who played a pivotal role in the 2022/2023 campaign, has returned as deputy director-general for election planning, coordination and monitoring.

Faleke, according to the statement, will work with zonal directors, including Senator Olushola Adeyeye in the South-west; Dr Ngozi Olejeme in the South-South; Senator Uche Ekwunife in the South-east; Muntaqha Rabe in the North-west; Ahmed Muhammed Ketso in the North-central; and Senator Sani Danladi in the North-east.



Similarly, Ms Stella Okotete, Abdullahi Garba Ramat and Audu Maikori will serve as secretaries of the election planning directorate.

Muiz Adeyemi Banire will lead the legal directorate as director, with Dr. Liman Hassan and Babatunde Ogala as deputies.

The statement identified the other members of the legal directorate to include: Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi; former governor of Katsina State, Ibrahim Shema; Worgu Boms; and Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh.



The statement also explained that the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris Malagi, will serve as the Coordinating Director for Media and Strategic Communication, alongside Dele Alake, Onanuga, and Lanre Issa-Onilu.

The media directorate also includes Tunde Rahman, Sunday Dare, Daniel Bwala, and Felix Morka, who have been assigned as coordinating deputy directors.



Abdulaziz AbdulAziz will work with three others, namely Temitope Ajayi, Arabinrin Aderonke, and Frederick Nwabufor, as coordinating secretaries of the media directorate.

Segun Dada will serve as Director, New Media, the same role he performed in 2022, while Solomon Arowolo will serve as Secretary, New Media.



The campaign council also appointed five spokespersons, led by Dele Alake. Other spokespersons are Alwan Hassan, Ayobami Oyalowo, Kemi Asekun-Shittu and Adamu Fanda.

Yari Accepts Appointment as Campaign Council DG

Meanwhile, Senator Yari has accepted his appointment as Director-General of the APC Campaign Council for the 2027 election.

Yari, who represents Zamfara West in the Senate, expressed gratitude to President Tinubu and the APC leadership for entrusting him with the responsibility.



“I accept this responsibility with deep gratitude and full seriousness.

“My sincere thanks go to President Bola Tinubu and the party for the trust placed in me, and to our party leadership for the confidence. I do not take it lightly,” Yari said.



He described the campaign as more than an electoral contest, saying it would be “a conversation with the Nigerian people in every state, every language, every faith about the future we are building together.”

The former Zamfara State governor pledged to conduct the campaign with discipline, unity and respect for all Nigerians, adding that work would begin immediately.



Yari also called on Nigerians across political divides to choose progress over division, saying the APC would seek to earn public confidence through its record rather than “noise.”

“By the grace of God, and with the effort of us all, we will deliver victory in January 2027,” he concluded.

ADC: APC Campaign Council a Rehabilitation Centre for Corruption Suspects

Meanwhile, the ADC has described the APC campaign council as a “rehabilitation centre” for persons facing unresolved corruption questions.

In a statement by the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the party questioned the inclusion of former officials Betta Edu and Ngozi Olejeme, calling on the government to disclose whether outstanding corruption cases involving them had been resolved or if this appointment is Tinubu’s way of pardoning corrupt officials affiliated with his party.



The ADC spokesman argued that most of the individuals assembled for the President’s campaign lacked credibility, insisting that the 2027 general election will be a referendum on Tinubu’s performance over the last three years.



Abdullahi said: ”We have taken note of the composition of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s 2027 campaign council. What should ordinarily be a political task team ends up looking like a rehabilitation system for individuals carrying unresolved questions of corruption and public accountability.



”We note, especially, the inclusion of former Humanitarian Affairs Minister, Betta Edu, who President Tinubu suspended following the controversy surrounding the attempted transfer of N585 million into a private account, as well as Former NSITF Chairman Ngozi Olejeme, who has faced EFCC prosecution over allegations of financial malpractices, among others whose names carry a pungent odour of corruption.

World.title: Al Jama-ah leader slams Adam Habib’s endorsement of Helen Zille for Joburg mayor
World.content:
Al Jama-ah leader Ganief Hendricks has criticised former Wits University vice-chancellor Adam Habib for endorsing Democratic Alliance (DA) candidate Helen Zille for the Johannesburg mayoral position.

Zille, the former Western Cape premier, is the DA’s mayoral candidate for South Africa’s economic hub and one of the country’s most closely contested metropolitan municipalities, the City of Johannesburg.

Her campaign has sought to highlight what the party describes as severe service delivery failures in the municipality. Among the campaign activities, Zille has been filmed swimming in a pothole-filled area, playing tennis on a court with overgrown grass and highlighting infrastructure failures across the city.



ADAM HABIB ENDORSES HELEN ZILLE FOR JOHANNESBURG MAYOR

Taking to X, Habib shared an article highlighting the financial challenges facing businesses in Johannesburg, including concerns about economic conditions in the city.

Habib said it was important for Helen Zille to win decisively and be elected mayor, arguing that this was what Johannesburg needed.

“Helen defined this election from day 1 with her performative campaigning & her service delivery focus. Everyone else responds to her, reflected even in the racist diatribes. My fear is that she will get the largest vote but not the majority and then the other politicians gang up,” he wrote.

He added: “The ganging up of politicians against Helen to keep her from power even though she has the largest vote will not be an example of democracy. It will show that racism, chauvinism and personal agendas have won out against the collective good. JHB will suffer as it has for years.”

AL JAMA-AH LEADER WEIGHS IN

Reacting to the endorsement, Hendricks said Habib “does not know what he is talking about”.

Hendricks, who is also the Deputy Minister of Social Development, said the DA had been given two opportunities to lead the City of Johannesburg but had failed, which he argued contributed to governance and financial instability in the municipality.



“The DA had two chances and failed twice. Johannesburg cannot afford a third experiment,” he said.

The DA has governed Johannesburg during two separate periods in recent years. Herman Mashaba served as mayor from 2016 to 2019, while Mpho Phalatse served as mayor from 2021 to 2023.

Hendricks also criticised Helen Zille’s previous role within the DA, claiming that the party “systematically dismantled Johannesburg’s administration” while she served as Federal Council chairperson.

“Now, she returns to finish the job and sabotage the City’s rightful vision to stand as the iconic economic beacon of Africa,” he said.

Touching on what he described as the DA’s track record in Johannesburg, Hendricks cited alleged staff purges, alleged illegal spying through the Group Forensic and Investigative Services, and the collapse of small and medium-sized enterprises allegedly linked to unpaid municipal contracts, among other issues.

Hendricks’ comments come as political parties intensify their campaigns ahead of the 4 November local government elections, with Johannesburg expected to be one of the key battlegrounds.

World.title: Power outages hit several Durban areas after intense windstorm
World.content:
Strong winds have caused severe damages and power outages in parts of Durban. Image: eThekwini Municipality / Facebook

Strong winds across Durban have left several communities without electricity after damaging overhead power infrastructure on Saturday afternoon, 22 August 2026.

The eThekwini Municipality’s Electricity and Energy Directorate is currently attending to multiple outages, with technical teams working to restore electricity to areas that remain affected.

Strong winds damage electricity infrastructure

According to the municipality, most of the outages occurred on overhead medium-voltage (OHM) circuits, which are particularly vulnerable during periods of strong winds.



Tree branches and other objects blown by the wind, including roof sheets, can damage overhead electricity lines and equipment, resulting in power outages.

Affected areas include:

Baphehli

Folweni

Amaoti

Waterloo

Moriah

Klaarwater

Savannah Park

Inanda

Gunjini

Redcliffe

Malukazi

KwaNdengezi

Clermont

Umlazi C

Thornwood

The municipality said other areas may also be affected.



Electricity restoration underway

The municipality said that technical teams worked through the night following the outages, and electricity has already been restored to several affected communities around Durban.

Teams remain deployed across the city and are working through the outstanding faults to bring the remaining areas back online.

However, the municipality warned that restoring power after damage to overhead lines can take time.



“The restoration of electricity supply can take time, as switching staff and technical teams are required to inspect the affected overhead line circuits to identify the cause of the fault.” the municipality said.

Once the problem has been located, repairs must be completed before electricity can safely be restored.

This means some residents may remain without power while teams work through the backlog.



The municipality has also urged residents to stay away from fallen or damaged electricity infrastructure.

Durban residents should report damaged electricity equipment or fallen lines through the municipality’s official electricity fault-reporting channels rather than approaching or attempting to move the infrastructure themselves.

World.title: The ‘curse’ of the Springbok centurion club
World.content:
To date, 958 players have pulled the famed green and gold jersey over the heads, but only 10 have gone on to play at least 100 matches. Image: Franck Fife/AFP

Damian De Allende became just the 10th Springbok player to join the 100-Test centurion club on Saturday against the All Blacks at Ellis Park in Newlands.

To date, 958 players have pulled the famed green and gold jersey over the heads, but only 10 have gone on to play at least 100 matches.

For five of those 10 players, the milestone has been spoiled by defeat, while five others have walked away winners on the day.



SURVEY | Rate the referee and TMO: Springboks vs All Blacks

Three players played their 100th Test outside of South Africa, while four ‘raised their bat’ against the All Blacks, two against the Wallabies and one each against England, Wales, France and Italy.

Curiously, no Springbok has scored a point in their 100th Test.

Full list of Springbok centurions

Percy Montgomery became the first ever Springbok centurion on 16 August 2008 when he started at fullback against the All Blacks at Newlands, a stone’s throw away from his alma mater, SACS.

The Springboks lost 19-0.

Montgomery was 34 at the time.



He ended his career with 102 Tests to his name and a record-to-this-day 893 points, thanks to 25 tries, 153 conversions, 148 penalties and six drop goals.

John Smit was the second Springbok to play 100 Tests when he captained the side on 21 August 2010 against the All Blacks at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

The Springboks lost 29-22.

Smit, who started at hooker that day, was 32 at the time.

He ended his career with 111 Tests to his name and 40 points thanks to eight tries.

Victor Matfield was the third Springbok to reach 100 Tests, with his milestone coming just a week (28 August 2010) after John Smit, this time against the Wallabies at his beloved Loftus Versfeld in Pretoria.

The Springboks won 44-31, with Matfield, who started at lock, 33 years old on the day.

Matfield, who hung up his boots after 127 Tests, scored 35 points for the Springboks thanks to seven tries.

Bryan Habana was the fourth Springbok to reach 100 Tests in the green and gold, with his milestone coming on 6 September 2014 against the Wallabies at the then Subiaco Oval in Perth.

The Springboks lost 24-23, with Habana 31 on the day.

He ended his career after 124 Tests and still holds the record of 67 tries for the Springboks, giving him the fourth-highest number of Test points with 335.

Jean de Villiers became the fifth Springbok Test centurion on 13 September 2014, just a week after Bryan Habana reached the milestone.

De Villiers’ 100th Test came against the All Blacks at the then Wellington Regional Stadium in Wellington, a match the Springboks lost 14-10.

He was 33 on the day of the Test and started at inside centre.

De Villiers played 109 Tests in total, scoring 135 points via 27 tries.

Tendai ‘Beast’ Mtawarira became the sixth Springbok to play 100 Tests and the first prop to do so.

Born in Harare in Zimbabwe, Mtawarira’s 100th Test came on 16 June 2018 against England at the Free State Stadium in Bloemfontein.

The Springboks won the match 23-12 with Mtawarira, who played his rugby as a loosehead prop, 32 on the day.

He played a total of 117 Tests, scoring 10 points via two tries.

Eben Etzebeth became the seventh – and youngest to date – Springbok to play 100 Tests when he ran out at lock at the Cape Town Stadium at age 30 against Wales on 16 July 2022.

The Springboks won the match 30-14.

Making the occasion extra-special, was the fact that Etzebeth’s wife, Anlia, sang the national anthem prior to kick-off.

Etzebeth has to date played 143 Tests, the most for the Springboks and the sixth-most of all time.

He has scored 45 points via nine tries.

Willie le Roux became the eighth player to play 100 Tests for the Springboks when he did so from fullback against Italy on 12 July 2025 at the Nelson Mandela Bay Stadium in Gqeberha.

He had the least stressful 100th Test, with the Springboks winning 45-0.

Le Roux was 35 on the day, making him the oldest Springbok to play his 100th Test.

Although still active, Le Roux isn’t currently part of the Springbok set-up.

He has scored 75 points via 15 tries in his 101 Tests to date.

Siya Kolisi became the ninth Springbok to play 100 Tests when he captained the side from flank against France at the Stade de France in Paris on 8 November 2025.

The Springboks won the match 32-17.

Kolisi was 34 at the time of the match.

To date, Kolisi has played 104 Tests, scoring 70 points via 14 tries.

Damian de Allende became the 10th and most recent Springbok centurion on 22 August 2026 against the All Blacks at Ellis Park in Johannesburg.

The Springboks lost the match 33-16.

De Allende, who was 34 on match-day, started at inside centre.

He has scored 55 points for the Springboks via 11 tries, but hasn’t scored in his last 25 Tests.

Pieter-Steph du Toit, with 99 Test caps, is next in line to join the centurion club, potentially in Cape Town next weekend. Time will tell whether he’s a winner – or loser – on that occasion.

Others in line to reach triple figures in the not so distance future are Jesse Kriel (91 Tests), Malcolm Marx (90 Tests) and Handre Pollard (87 Tests).

How many of the above 100th Test matches do you recall?

World.title: Sekhukhune United 0-1 Orlando Pirates: 5 key worries for the Buccaneers
World.content:
Orlando Pirates managed to scrape past Sekhukhune United at the old Peter Mokaba Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

A first-half goal from Deon Hotto was enough to give the Buccaneers a 1-0 victory in the first leg of their MTN8 semi-final.

Pirates will now return to Orlando Amstel Arena with a slender advantage and will be favourites to reach yet another final.



However, despite the important win, there were still a few areas of concern for the Buccaneers.

Here are five things Orlando Pirates will need to address:

Sebelebele’s defending

Mike Mamosha often leaves gaps when he pushes forward, and on several occasions he was caught out of position against Sekhukhune.



His defensive ability has already come under scrutiny. Against AmaZulu, he conceded a penalty after being caught out, highlighting an area Pirates may need to address.

Lack of creativity in midfield

With Patrick Tito Maswanganyi having left the club, Pirates no longer have the same creative spark in midfield.

That could become a major problem as the season progresses. Against Sekhukhune, the Buccaneers often looked flat and struggled to find solutions when they had possession.



They will need someone to step up and provide the creativity that Maswanganyi previously offered.

Orlando Pirates need to replace TITO ASAP

Pedersen needs to improve

Norwegian striker Sebastian Pedersen finally made his debut, but his performance did little to suggest that he will immediately solve Pirates’ goalscoring problems.

He had a golden opportunity to open his account but fired wide. Aside from that chance, he struggled to make a significant impact in the final third.



Orlando Pirates will need much more from their new striker, particularly with a demanding season ahead.

Mbatha is needed

Camren Dansin has impressed since breaking into the team, but the youngster is still a work in progress.

With the Buccaneers competing on multiple fronts, the experience and quality of players such as Thalente Mbatha and Makhehlene Makhaula will be important.



This will be especially true in CAF matches, where Pirates will need experienced midfielders capable of controlling difficult games.

No super subs

In the matches they played, there has never been a match winner from the bench and new signings are not giving Ouaddou a lot to work with.

Orlando Pirates have made a strong start to the campaign, but Saturday’s victory also showed that there are still areas that need improvement.



With the MTN8 final now within touching distance, the Buccaneers will hope to fix those weaknesses before the second leg.

Can the Buccaneers win the MTN8?

World.title: Orlando Pirates transfer news: Tito, Witbooi, Van Rooyen, Matuludi
World.content:
Orlando Pirates are reportedly set to part ways with Patrick ‘Tito’ Maswanganyi in the coming days.

The potential departure of the 28-year-old midfielder comes as a surprise, especially after he started the season in good form for the Buccaneers.

There have been rumours that Maswanganyi and Pirates head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou have not always seen eye to eye, although neither the player nor the club has publicly confirmed those claims.



SABC Sport reported that Maswanganyi is closing in on a move to Bahrain after he was left out of the Orlando Pirates squad for Saturday’s MTN8 semi-final first-leg victory over Sekhukhune United.

“It’s believed the Soweto giants have all but concluded talks with an as-yet unnamed club in the Asian Football Confederation (AFC),” the publication reported.

Ouaddou was asked about Maswanganyi’s absence after the victory but refused to go into detail.



“For the other player I cannot say too much about the issue, he’s not injured,” the Pirates coach said.

“He was available but I cannot speak about something that I don’t masterise in.”

Tito to leave Orlando Pirates

Maswanganyi’s potential exit could be one of the biggest surprises of the transfer window, with the midfielder having played an important role for Pirates since joining the club.



While Maswanganyi could be heading out, Pirates could also be preparing to strengthen their squad.

The Buccaneers have been linked with Polokwane City right-back Thabang Matuludi.

The defender has reportedly not been training or featuring for Rise and Shine, fuelling speculation that he could be on his way out of the club.



Orlando Pirates recently parted ways with Deano van Rooyen, potentially opening up an opportunity for the club to bring in another right-back.

Matuludi could therefore emerge as a possible replacement as Pirates continue to reshape their squad.

Another player linked with a move to Orlando Pirates is teenage sensation Emile Witbooi.



However, reports suggest the highly rated youngster could instead be heading to Bayern Munich for trials.

For now, Maswanganyi’s situation remains the biggest talking point, with Pirates potentially set to lose one of their talented midfielders just weeks into the new season.

Should Pirates release Tito?

World.title: Mitchells Plain area where the average home sells for R1.4 million
World.content:
Cape Town’s housing landscape is changing.

As of 2026, the average home price in Cape Town is R2.3 million; in the Western Cape, it’s R1.8 million.

In Mitchells Plain, the average house price is R780 000.



For one area within its boundaries, home prices are nearly double that.

Mitchells Plain’s Affluent Suburb

Mitchells Plain isn’t one homogeneous area.

Rather, it’s divided into sub-areas, each with a unique characteristic.

Affluent buyers are drawn to some of these areas, where the community feel is welcoming and friendly.

It’s not only the community vibe, but also the value for money.

According to Property24, two Mitchells Plain suburbs have home prices averaging above R1.3 million, but only one has surpassed R1.4 million.



That area is Westgate, where the average home sells for R1.41 million.

Younger buyers, in particular, find the area appealing.

As of 2026, buyers under 50 make up 100% of the sales.

Buyers between 18 and 35 make up 66.7% of the sales, while the remaining 33.3% are between 36 and 49.

Currently, the most affordable house listed in Westgate is a 2-bedroom home on auction with a R1.25 million reserve.

One 6-bedroom home in Westgate is listed for R2.2 million.

Westgate first crossed the R1 million mark in 2021, before briefly dipping below that figure in 2022.

Prices in the area have been steadily increasing ever since.

Strandfontein Homes Average R1.3 million

Westgate isn’t the only area in Mitchells Plain’s affluent bracket.

In Strandfontein, part of the broader Mitchells Plain census area, the average home price is R1 347 000 as of 2026.

The area, along False Bay, offers buyers a coastal lifestyle without the typical coastal price.

Take neighbouring Pelican Heights for example.

The average house price in this coastal suburb has reached R2.3 million, with land selling for R1.69 million.

Properties in Strandfontein are 41.4% cheaper.

That cost reduction, along with beach access and proximity to two nature reserves, appeals to younger buyers, who make up 77.8% of transactions in the region.

What’s Next for Mitchells Plain?

Mitchells Plain is currently home to five areas where the average property price is above R1 million.

Areas like Colorado Park and Mandalay have an average sale price above R1.2 million.

Westridge, which neighbours Westgate, currently falls just below the R1 million threshold.

The average sale price in the area is R927 000.

But it may be the next up-and-coming suburb.

Mitchells Plain’s Affluent Areas

World.title: UPDATED | Top 10 most-capped Test players list

Veteran lock Eben Etzebeth has extended his record as the most capped Springbok of all time to 143 Test matches. Image: SA Rugby website

Saturday’s opening ‘Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’ Test between the Springboks and All Blacks at Ellis Park saw veteran South Africa lock Eben Etzebeth claim sole possession of sixth place in the list of most Tests played.

Etzebeth has now played 143 Tests and finds himself one ahead of now-retired Italian No 8, Sergio Parisse.

SURVEY | Rate the referee and TMO: Springboks vs All Blacks



The 34-year-old also closed the gap on All Blacks utility back Beauden Barrett who was not selected in the All Blacks’ matchday 23-man squad.

Barrett currently has 144 caps to his name.

Retired Wales and British & Irish Lions lock Alun Wyn Jones leads the way with 170 overall Test matches played.



There is plenty of time for Etzebeth to further climb the list before he hangs up his studs.

Latest centurion

For the record, there have been 958 Springboks to date.



De Allende joined an illustrious list of South African centurions which includes Etzebeth (143*), Victor Matfield (127), Bryan Habana (124), ‘Beast’ Mtawarira (117), John Smit (111), Jean de Villiers (109), Siya Kolisi (104*), Percy Montgomery (102) and Willie le Roux (101*).
